202	**Key point.** What actually fires is decided by four interacting semantics, per Field, independently, all in one pass: a **Term** matches its words in any casing and however they are spaced (whitespace collapses to `\s+`) but only where it stands as a word, with a hyphen and an underscore counting as *inside* a word; a **Symbol** is one code point matched anywhere, unless `flanked='whitespace'`, where the edge of the Field counts as whitespace; and an **Exception** suppresses a firing only where the match falls **wholly inside** a span the Exception covers, and only for the one Rule it hangs off.
203	
204	**Ground truth.**
205	- `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/src/violation.ts` (`findViolations` 28–56, `suppressedSpans` 71–73, `isSuppressed` 81–85, `termViolations` 88–104, `matcherFor` 123–127, `standsAsWord` 134–136, `isOutsideAWord` 143–145, `symbolViolations` 148–165, `flankedByWhitespace` 172–174, `isGap` 177–179)
206	- `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/src/rule-set.ts` (`TermRule`/`SymbolRule`/`RuleIdentity` 67–92, `checkStoredRule` 125–179)
207	- `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/schema.sql` (`a_symbol_is_one_character`, `only_a_symbol_is_flanked`, `field_belongs_to_the_content`)
208	- `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/default-rules.sql` (74 Terms lines 53–139, 15 Symbols lines 154–185, the five-Field cross join, the honesty note at 195–217)

210	**Mechanism.** `findViolations(content, ruleSets)` walks `Map<Field, RuleSet>`, skips a Field the content does not carry (`preconditions` optional), and for each Rule computes `fired` then `suppressed = suppressedSpans(value, rule.exceptions)` — that Rule's Exceptions alone — and filters. `matcherFor` escapes regex metacharacters then replaces `\s+` runs with `\\s+`, flags `giu`. `termViolations` keeps only spans where `standsAsWord`, which tests the characters either side against `/[\p{L}\p{N}_-]/u`, `undefined` (Field edge) counting as outside. The reported `text` is the casing **found**, with `offset` its start. `symbolViolations` uses `indexOf` in a loop, applying `flankedByWhitespace` when `rule.flanked === 'whitespace'`, with `isGap(undefined) === true`. `isSuppressed` requires `offset >= span.start && offset + text.length <= span.end`. "One character" is enforced twice with the same reading: `looks_for like '_'` in Postgres, and `[...looksFor].length !== 1` in `checkStoredRule` — both count code points, so an em dash passes and a glyph carrying a variation selector does not. `default-rules.sql` cross-joins 89 checks against five Fields, producing 445 independent Rules; there is no inheritance and no cross-field Rule.

212	**Why it matters.** This is what a caller experiences as "the validator". And 445 Rules on five Fields means the wrong answer arrives 445 times.

## #1

**Key point.** Every write travels three refusals in a fixed order — Fastify JSON Schema, then the bound Rules, then the `testlink-mcp` call — and nothing reaches TestLink until all three clear; reads travel none of them and are never refused, carrying what fired beside the content they serve. The three refusals answer in three distinguishable shapes (`400 {refusal:'schema'}`, `422 {violations}`, `404 {message}`), so a caller never has to read a string to know which stage stopped it.

**Ground truth.**
- `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/src/app.ts` (whole file; schemas 26–126, `reject` 179–185, `setErrorHandler` 188–193, `nothingThere` 201–202, routes 204–431)
- `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/src/violation.ts`
- `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/src/testlink-client.ts` (`TestLinkClient`, 91–125)
- `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/src/server.ts` (79–88, composition)

**Mechanism.** `buildApp({testlink, documents, rules, logger})` builds Fastify with `ajv.customOptions.coerceTypes: false`. `testCaseSchema` (`required: ['name','summary']`, `additionalProperties: false`) is attached as `schema.body` on `POST /projects/:projectId/suites/:suiteId/test-cases` and `PUT /test-cases/:id`. A schema failure reaches `setErrorHandler`, which sees `error.validation` and answers `400 {refusal:'schema', message}` — carrying no `violations` key, so it cannot be misread as a Rejection. Otherwise `findViolations(request.body, bound.testCase)` runs; a non-empty array goes to `reject()`, which emits one `request.log.warn({ruleSetVersion, field, rule}, 'Rule violated')` per Violation and answers `422 versioned({violations})`. Only then is `testlink.createTestCase`/`updateTestCase` called. `undefined`/`false` back from the client becomes `nothingThere(reply, ...)` → `404 {message: 'TestLink holds no ...'}`. Success is `201 versioned(written)` or `200 versioned({id})`. Reads (`GET /test-cases/:id`, `GET /reference-documents/:id`) call `findViolations` too but always send `200` with `{testCase|document, violations}` — Violations sit beside the content, never merged into it. `GET/POST/PUT/DELETE` on `/projects` and `/projects/:projectId/suites/...` run schema only: no Rule binds to a Project or a Suite.

**Why it matters.** This ordering is the product. If the Rules stage could be reached after the write, or if a Rejection could be confused with a schema refusal or with absence, the whole trust-boundary argument collapses — the agent would have a way to get unchecked prose into TestLink, or a way to read "not there" as "rejected" and stop trying.

**Diagram.**
```
 agent (HTTP)
     │
     ▼  POST /projects/:projectId/suites/:suiteId/test-cases
 ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ (1) Fastify ajv, testCaseSchema, coerceTypes:false      │
 │     fail ──► setErrorHandler ──► 400 {refusal:'schema'} │──┐
 ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤  │
 │ (2) findViolations(body, bound.testCase)                │  │ nothing
 │     len>0 ──► reject(): log.warn ×n ──► 422 {violations}│──┤ written
 ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤  │
 │ (3) testlink.createTestCase(...)  ── undefined ──► 404  │──┘
 │                                   ── {id}      ──► 201  │──► TestLink
 └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

 GET /test-cases/:id ── no refusal stage ──► 200 {testCase, violations}
 GET /reference-documents/:id ─────────────► 200 {document, violations}
```

**Contradicts.** Nothing. README lines 3–6, 220–231 and 344–346 describe exactly this ordering and these two response shapes.

## #2

**Key point.** Startup is the gate, and after it the database is a read-only input that no request can change. The server reads its Rules from `rules`/`rule_exceptions` **once**, refuses to start on a missing setting, on an empty result, or on any row it cannot bind — and afterwards nothing in the process can write a Rule or a Reference Document, so the `Rule-Set-Version` derived from those rows is fixed for the life of the process and rides on every single answer.

**Ground truth.**
- `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/src/server.ts` (12–26 read-once and the empty refusal; 40–68 `testLinkMcp()`; 70–88)
- `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/src/setting.ts`
- `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/src/postgres-store.ts` (`hasSchema` 17–23, `exceptionsByRule` 31–50, `rules` 77–98, `getDocument` 106–113, `connectToPostgres` 140–146)

- `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/schema.sql`, `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/default-rules.sql`

**Mechanism.** `server.ts` top-level `await`s: `connectToPostgres(required('DATABASE_URL'))` → `new PostgresStore(...)` → `await store.rules()`. `rules()` first asks `select 1 from information_schema.tables where table_name='rules'` (`hasSchema`) so an un-applied schema answers `[]` rather than throwing; then `select ... from rules where enabled order by id` plus a separate `select rule, phrase from rule_exceptions where enabled order by id` folded into a `Map<number,string[]>` keyed by `rules.id`. Zero rows → the explicit `throw new Error('No enabled Rules are in the database, so the server will not start. Apply schema.sql and insert a Rule ...')`. Inside `buildApp`, `bindRules(rules)` runs `checkStoredRule` over every row and `refuse()`s with *all* problems joined, before Fastify exists. `ruleSetVersionOf(rules)` is a sha256 sliced to 12 hex chars over `JSON.stringify([contentKind, field, ruleId, category, looksFor, flanked, reason, sortedExceptions])` per row, `.sort()`ed then newline-joined — so row `id` and database ordering are excluded, and disabled rows never reach it. An `onSend` hook stamps `Rule-Set-Version` on *every* reply including the `204`s; `versioned()` puts `ruleSetVersion` in the body only where Rules took part. The write direction is absent by construction: `PostgresStore` has `rules`, `listDocuments`, `getDocument` and nothing else; `DocumentStore` declares only the two reads. `schema.sql` and `default-rules.sql` are operator-applied (`psql -f`), never referenced from `src/`.

**Why it matters.** Two guarantees stand on this and nothing else: a running server cannot be talked into loosening a Rule (there is no object in the process that can write one), and a Violation reported today can still be explained tomorrow (the version names the exact Rules that judged it). **Mechanism.** `connectToTestLinkMcp` spawns the MCP server over `StdioClientTransport` and flattens its reply to `{text, isError}` — the only structural signal there is. `McpTestLinkClient.answer(tool, args, alsoTheCallers?)` calls it, then: `isError` → `place(tool, text, alsoTheCallers)`; otherwise `JSON.parse(result.text)` and `reportedProblem(content)` (first element carrying both a `code` and a string `message`) → `place(...)`; then `deniedIn(content)` (`status === false`) → `throw 'TestLink did not complete <tool>: ...'`; otherwise the content. `place` tries, in order: `alsoTheCallers` → `unconfirmed`; `reportsMissingTool` (`/Unknown tool/i`) → `throw 'testlink-mcp does not provide <tool>, so it is older than the 1.6.0 this client calls'`; `reportsAbsence` (`/does not exist|not found/i`) → `absent`; else `throw 'TestLink could not be reached through <tool>: ...'`. `deleteProject` is the only call passing `alsoTheCallers = reportsUnconfirmed` (`/Confirmation failed/i`) and answers the three-valued `ProjectDeletion`. `idOf` reads `first(content).id ?? first(content).additionalInfo.id` and throws when missing, `''` or `0`. `listProjects` and `createProject` treat `absent` as nonsense and throw. In `app.ts`: `absent` → `404` via `nothingThere`, `'unconfirmed'` → `409`, every throw → Fastify `500`.

**Why it matters.** These are the only failures the caller cannot see the cause of, and every one is decided by matching a *string another program produced*. Two regexes (`does not exist|not found`, `Confirmation failed`) carry the whole difference between "correct your id" (404), "restate the prefix" (409) and "escalate, TestLink is down" (500). A stub written to emit those strings proves the regex matches the stub — nothing more.

**Diagram.**
```
 route ──► McpTestLinkClient.<op> ──► ToolCaller.call(tool,args)
                                          │  {text, isError}
                                          ▼
                            ┌── isError ──► place()
   JSON.parse(text) ────────┤
        │                   └── reportedProblem(): {code, message} ──► place()
        ▼
   deniedIn(): status===false ─────────────────► throw ──► 500
        │
        └── content ───────────────────────────────────► 200/201
                                 (create: idOf() no id ─► throw ─► 500)

   place(message):
     reportsUnconfirmed /Confirmation failed/i ─► unconfirmed ─► 409
     reportsMissingTool /Unknown tool/i        ─► throw "older than 1.6.0" ─► 500
     reportsAbsence /does not exist|not found/i─► absent      ─► 404 nothingThere
     anything else                             ─► throw "could not be reached" ─► 500
```

**Contradicts.** Nothing. README lines 263–275 and 332–340 describe this exactly, including the `1.6.0` pin, which matches `expectedTestLinkMcp` and the tag in `.mcp.json.example`.

## #4

**Key point.** What actually fires is decided by four interacting semantics, per Field, independently, in one pass: a **Term** matches its words in any casing and however spaced (whitespace collapses to `\s+`) but only where it stands as a word, with hyphen and underscore counting as *inside* a word; a **Symbol** is one code point matched anywhere, unless `flanked='whitespace'`, where the Field edge counts as whitespace; and an **Exception** suppresses a firing only where the match falls **wholly inside** a span it covers, and only for the one Rule it hangs off.

**Ground truth.**
- `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/src/violation.ts` (`findViolations` 28–56, `suppressedSpans` 71–73, `isSuppressed` 81–85, `termViolations` 88–104, `matcherFor` 123–127, `standsAsWord` 134–136, `isOutsideAWord` 143–145, `symbolViolations` 148–165, `flankedByWhitespace` 172–174, `isGap` 177–179)
- `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/src/rule-set.ts` (`TermRule`/`SymbolRule`/`RuleIdentity` 67–92, `checkStoredRule` 125–179)
- `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/schema.sql` (`a_symbol_is_one_character`, `only_a_symbol_is_flanked`, `field_belongs_to_the_content`)
- `/home/jack/src/testcase-validator/default-rules.sql` (74 Terms 53–139, 15 Symbols 154–185, the five-Field cross join, the honesty note 195–217)

**Mechanism.** `findViolations(content, ruleSets)` walks `Map<Field, RuleSet>`, skips a Field the content does not carry (`preconditions` optional), and per Rule computes `fired` then `suppressed = suppressedSpans(value, rule.exceptions)` — that Rule's Exceptions alone — and filters. `matcherFor` escapes regex metacharacters then replaces `\s+` runs with `\\s+`, flags `giu`. `termViolations` keeps only spans where `standsAsWord`, testing the characters either side against `/[\p{L}\p{N}_-]/u`, `undefined` (Field edge) counting as outside. The reported `text` is the casing **found**, `offset` its start. `symbolViolations` uses `indexOf` in a loop, applying `flankedByWhitespace` when `rule.flanked === 'whitespace'`, with `isGap(undefined) === true`. `isSuppressed` requires `offset >= span.start && offset + text.length <= span.end`. "One character" is enforced twice with the same reading: `looks_for like '_'` in Postgres and `[...looksFor].length !== 1` in `checkStoredRule` — both count code points, so an em dash passes and a glyph carrying a variation selector does not. `default-rules.sql` cross-joins 89 checks against five Fields, producing 445 independent Rules; no inheritance, no cross-field Rule.

**Why it matters.** This is what a caller experiences as "the validator". Every boundary has a plausible wrong answer that would look identical in a green suite — `utilises` flagged, `re-associates` flagged, a phrase silently defeated by a line break, an Exception written for one Rule quietly suppressing another. And 445 Rules on five Fields means the wrong answer arrives 445 times.

**Diagram.**
```
 content {name, summary, preconditions}   bound.testCase: Map<Field, RuleSet>
        │                                        │
        └──────────► per Field, per Rule ◄───────┘
                           │
        ┌──────────────────┴──────────────────┐
        ▼ term                                ▼ symbol
  matcherFor: escape, \s+→\s+, /giu     indexOf loop over looks_for
        │                                     │
  standsAsWord? chars either side       flanked==='whitespace'?
  in [\p{L}\p{N}_-] ──yes──► skip         │yes── isGap(l) && isGap(r)?
        │no                                │        (edge counts as gap)
        ▼                                  ▼no──► fires anywhere
   fires: {field, rule, reason, text(as found), offset}
        │
        ▼  suppressedSpans(value, THIS rule's exceptions only)
   isSuppressed: offset >= start && offset+len <= end ──► dropped
        │
        ▼
   Violation[] — every Field, every Rule, one pass, no short circuit

   "utilise"   vs "utilises"    ─► no fire      (standsAsWord)
   "associates" vs "re-associates" ─► no fire   (- is inside a word)
   "let's dive in" split over a newline ─► fires (\s+)
   "-" flanked  : "a - b" fires; "well-known" does not; "- x" fires
```

**Contradicts.** Nothing. CONTEXT.md's **Term**, **Symbol**, **Flanking** and **Exception** entries and README lines 212–217 describe precisely these semantics.

**Paths.**

- **4a.** Rule `('no-utilise','term','utilise')`; submit `summary: "The client utilises the AP"` → **no** Violation → **the case is written and TestLink holds it**. Detection half *fake-assertable*; the written-through half *NOT fake-assertable*.
- **4b.** Same Rule; `summary: "Utilise the AP"` → one Violation whose `text` is `"Utilise"` at `offset 0`. *Fake-assertable.*
- **4c.** Rule term `associates`; `summary: "the client re-associates"` → no Violation. *Fake-assertable.*
- **4d.** Rule term `let's dive in`; summary carrying `let's\n  dive in` → fires, `text` spanning the newline. *Fake-assertable.*
- **4e.** Symbol Rule `'-'` with `flanked='whitespace'`: `"a - b"` fires; `"well-known"` does not; `"- start"` and `"end -"` fire. *Fake-assertable.*
- **4f.** Symbol Rule `'—'` with `flanked` null → fires inside a word too. *Fake-assertable.*
- **4g.** `insert ... category='symbol', looks_for='⚠️'` (two code points) → **`a_symbol_is_one_character` refuses the insert and the row is absent from `rules`**; the same value forced into an unconstrained table is refused at startup. *NOT fake-assertable* — asserts real Postgres `like '_'` character (not byte) semantics.
- **4h.** `insert ... category='term', flanked='whitespace'` → `only_a_symbol_is_flanked` refuses → **row absent**. *NOT fake-assertable.*
- **4i.** Rule `no-ap` (term `AP`) with Exception `AP isolation`; `preconditions: "AP isolation is on, and the AP is up"` → exactly one Violation, at the second `AP`. *Fake-assertable* — but see 4k.
- **4j.** Exception `guest-*`; content `guest-*1` → still fires. *Fake-assertable.*
- **4k.** Two Rules on one Field, an Exception inserted against Rule A's `id` → **Rule B still fires inside the excepted phrase** — proving `exceptionsByRule` keyed the phrase to the right `rules.id`. *NOT fake-assertable*: the id-to-phrase wiring only exists between two real tables.
- **4l.** A Rule disabled and one of its Exceptions still `enabled` → the Rule does not fire at all, and the orphan Exception changes nothing. *NOT fake-assertable.*
- **4m.** One submission violating three Rules across two Fields → the `422` lists **all three**. *Fake-assertable.*
- **4n.** Submit a Test Case with `preconditions` omitted → Rules bound to `preconditions` produce nothing, Rules on `name`/`summary` still run. *Fake-assertable.*
- **4o.** With the shipped 445 Rules applied to a real database and the server booted from them: `summary: "This will successfully verify that the AP works — as expected."` → Violations under `no-successfully`, `no-verify-that`, `no-em-dash`, `no-as-expected`, all bound to `summary` and none to `name` → **nothing written to TestLink**. *NOT fake-assertable.*
- **4p.** The six Terms holding a straight apostrophe (`in today's`, `let's dive in`, …) do **not** match the same phrase written with `’`; that content is caught under `no-curly-apostrophe` instead. *Fake-assertable* if the six real rows are loaded; *NOT fake-assertable* as a claim about the shipped file.

## Findings

**The second implementation.** `test/stub-testlink-client.ts` is 206 lines that reimplement TestLink. It mints ids (`testlink-${n}`, `project-${n}`, `suite-${n}`), holds three separate collections, and **enforces business rules**: `deleteProject` returns `'absent'`, `'unconfirmed'` or `'deleted'` by comparing a stored prefix; `createTestCase` returns `undefined` unless the suite was pre-held. The 404/409/500 tri-state that #3 says is the whole product is decided, in 17 of 18 files, by this file's `if` statements. There is no contract test binding it to a real TestLink. `pg-mem` is the same finding at the database seam, and ADR-0007 documents that its behaviour already diverges.

**The oracle test.** `test/postgres-store.test.ts` defines `StubQueries` whose own docstring says it *"answer[s] with rows a test supplies"*, then asserts `PostgresStore` returns those rows reshaped. `test/mcp-testlink-client.test.ts` does the same at a larger scale — `reports(value)` writes what testlink-mcp would say, and 46 tests assert the client's reading of text the test authored. Where these files assert a real fact they assert it about themselves.

**Islands.** Every test builds its own world and tears nothing down: `new StubTestLinkClient()` per test, `empty()` (a fresh pg-mem) per test, no shared fixture, no `afterEach`. Nothing is threaded because nothing is real enough to leak. The single exception proves it — the one counting test has `beforeAll`/`afterAll`, reuses fixtures by name across runs, and cleans up leftovers, precisely because its world persists.

**The one counting test is not in the repository.** `git status` reports `?? test/system-write-reaches-testlink.test.ts` — untracked. A fresh clone of this project has **0 of 58 paths asserted**, not 2. Every cell above except the fakes column depends on an uncommitted working-copy file.

**There is no CI, and `npm test` on a clean checkout is red by design.** No `.github` directory exists. `vitest run` collects the system test, which the file states *"fails rather than skips"* without `docker compose up -d`, both SQL files applied, and a populated `.env`. So the project's own test command cannot pass unattended, and there is no pipeline that would notice.

**A defect the counting test works around rather than reports.** Its `listed()` helper documents that TestLink answers "is empty" as an API failure, which `McpTestLinkClient` does not match, so an empty suite escalates as a `500`. The test absorbs this to reach its fixture — *"That is worth an issue of its own"* — so the suite's one real-infrastructure run has already found a #3 bug and routed around it.

## Verdict

**Passing proves the code agrees with fakes the same authors wrote — plus one real round-trip that is not in the repository.**
